findings.finding: Running genius's own base-case ranges through the contribution formula (price 18.99, referral 15% = 2.85, fba 3.45, storage 0.06, ads = ad_rate.base 0.42 x price = 7.98, returns = 0.05 x (0.4x18.99+0.6x4.44) = 0.51, landed 4.44) gives contribution = 18.99 - 19.29 = about -$0.30, i.e. NEGATIVE (-1.6% of price) -- not '25% red flag' or '15% no-go', but below zero. At ad_rate.low (0.22) contribution is only 18.4% of price (still below the 25% red-flag line); at ad_rate.high (0.70) it is deeply negative. So across nearly the whole supplied ad_rate range this 'FRAGILE MARGIN' product fails the contribution sanity rail, yet genius's three_sentences_to_founder[1] softens this to 'per-unit contribution runs close to zero on the base-case numbers' and feasibility_verdict stays 'stretch' with only landed-cost-vs-30% cited as passing. The founder-facing framing understates a base-case economics failure as a mild caution.
findings.fix: Let the engine confirm this from the supplied ranges, then state plainly (not softened) whether base-case contribution is negative; if so, either justify why a 42% blended year-1 ACoS is the right base case (vs. weighting more toward the 15-30% steady-state band), lower the ad_rate.base, cut cost, or explicitly reclassify feasibility toward 'unrealistic' rather than 'stretch' until the economics clear the no-go line.

findings.finding: The main_image prompt specifies 'background is a smooth muted sage-to-cream gradient sweep', and color_strategy.main_image_anchor confirms the intent: 'A muted sage-to-cream soft gradient background (not sterile white, not black)'. Amazon's main/primary listing image requires a pure white (RGB 255,255,255) background for standard categories including Pet Supplies -- no gradients, no lifestyle backdrops. Shipping this prompt as the actual main image risks image rejection or suppression at compliance review, which would erase the entire 'stand out in the grid' CTR strategy (I2's contrast mesh, I3's rim text) this plan is built around.
findings.fix: Reserve the sage-to-cream gradient look for the packaging and lifestyle images (both are appropriately backgrounded already). Rewrite the main_image prompt to a pure white, seamless background per Amazon policy, and let the sage-green body plus white contrast mesh (I2) do the anchoring against that white field instead of a colored backdrop.

findings.finding: Amazon product/review pages were blocked this session, so scout's price_ladder and competitors entirely come from Walmart listings (F3-F6) -- the true Amazon combo-set comparators (tafit, Ilofdsn, Niteangel, BFLCTTBD, Mollcouver named in F1/F2) have no price or rating data at all this run. Buyer's anchoring judgement ('The row I see runs $4.29-$10.17...', anchor_seen_usd: 10.17) treats this Walmart-sourced ladder as if it were the literal Amazon grid row, without flagging the marketplace mismatch -- a quiet upgrade of an unverified cross-marketplace proxy into a settled Amazon anchor that feeds directly into gate.price_vs_anchor and kahneman.anchoring reasoning, and downstream into genius's price_usd rationale.
findings.fix: Scout should tag each competitor entry with its marketplace and state explicitly that no Amazon-native price anchor exists this run. Buyer should treat the $4.29-$10.17/$10.17 figures as a directional, non-Amazon proxy with wider stated uncertainty rather than 'the row I see', until Amazon data is retrievable.

findings.finding: genius.premortem item 4 assigns 30% probability to the upgraded die-cut box + shaped inner tray pushing the packed product over the 8oz small-standard tier line, jumping the FBA fee to the next tier -- genius's own top-named packaging risk. But economics.fba_fee_usd (low 2.90 / base 3.45 / high 4.15) only widens the same-tier estimate by roughly +20%; it does not include a next-tier fee scenario at the high end, so the Monte-Carlo input doesn't actually carry the risk genius itself flags as the most consequential packaging failure mode.
findings.fix: Either fold an explicit tier-jump scenario into the high end of fba_fee_usd (price the next FBA size tier's fee), or state clearly in the assumption that the current range assumes the pin-gauge/scale-check mitigation succeeds and that a tier-jump remains an unmodeled tail risk.

findings.finding: The 'second, narrower snap-in 3mm mesh insert for tight corners' plus a replacement-SKU card is introduced outside the formal ideas[] array -- no idea_id, no kano_class, no prior_art_risk, no thumbnail_visibility, only an ad hoc 'dimes' cost tier -- and it is not listed in version_plan.v1_now or v2_later. genius's BOM for either version does not appear to price this extra mesh insert or card at all, so it is a costed feature that never got assigned to a version or budgeted.
findings.fix: Give it an idea_id, run it through the same TRIZ/ERRC/prior-art/thumbnail-test discipline as I1-I6, and place it explicitly in v1_now or v2_later so genius can cost it in the BOM (or drop it if it's aspirational scope, not actual v1 content).

findings.finding: I3 (shipped in v1_now) and I1 (deferred) both list N4 ('real proof it was tested on small-animal bedding', severity 4) in improves_needs, but the innovation playbook restricts idea-targeting to needs with severity >= 5, and target_spec.needs_targeted correctly excludes N4 (only N1-N3 listed). No real economic harm since I3 is 'free' cost tier, but it's an internal inconsistency between what target_spec claims is being funded and what the idea itself claims to serve.
findings.fix: Remove N4 from I3's (and I1's) improves_needs, or add a note in target_spec that N4 is addressed incidentally at zero marginal cost as a side effect, not as a funded target.

findings.finding: I3 is self-rated 'medium' thumbnail_visibility, which per the innovation playbook's own thumbnail test means it 'needs a callout or image three' -- i.e. not reliably legible at true ~300px grid-thumbnail size. Yet listing_implications.main_image_brief and image_prompts[0] both describe the embossed '3MM BEDDING MESH' rim text as 'readable' directly in the hero/main image. Embossed, non-contrasting text on a tray rim is very unlikely to actually read at thumbnail size, contradicting the idea's own visibility rating.
findings.fix: Don't rely on I3's embossed text being legible in the grid thumbnail; let I2's color-contrast mesh carry the thumbnail-level proof, and move the 'readable molded text' claim to a full-size listing detail image (2-6), consistent with I3's own 'medium' rating.

findings.finding: For the v1_plus_hero window-strip BOM line, genius states it ran its 'own one-off web search this run (not a scout fact_id, not authorized by any brief clause, just a component-price check)' citing weilinplastic.com, rapiddirect.com and protolabs.com. This directly violates the pipeline's sourcing discipline: 'Scout searches; everyone else cites scout's fact_ids.' It's transparently disclosed and limited to the deferred v1_plus_hero version (no impact on v1_now's economics), but it breaks the chain-of-custody the whole evidence rule depends on.
findings.fix: Strip the named-domain citations and either fall back to the knowledge-base rule-of-thumb only (as done for every other BOM line this run), or route an authorized request to scout next run and cite a real fact_id instead.

findings.finding: Two specific competitive claims have no scout fact_id backing: (1) 'The named competitors (F1, F3-F6) ship as a bagged single scoop with no window and no explanation card' -- scout never captured any packaging detail for any competitor; and (2, in color_strategy.main_image_anchor) '...white-background, black-plastic rivals filling the rest of the grid' -- scout's competitor descriptions never state plastic color. Both read as plausible but invented specifics dressed up as observed competitive facts.
findings.fix: Soften both to 'typical category convention, not independently confirmed this session,' or have scout actually capture competitor packaging/color detail before stating it as comparative fact.

findings.finding: price_usd (low 16.99 / base 18.99 / high 19.99) is only about 16% wide (low -10.5%, high +5.3% around base), materially narrower than the ~+/-30% guidance applied to every other uncertain figure this run, and it carries no downside scenario for the case where the 'visible proof' buyer requires to accept a price above her stated $12 no-reason ceiling doesn't land as intended in the actual photography.
findings.fix: Widen the low end toward buyer's $12-14 no-reason-ceiling band to give the Monte-Carlo a genuine downside price scenario, or explicitly document that price is being treated as a fixed strategic decision rather than an uncertain input (and if so, why a range is supplied at all).

findings.finding: The optimistic tail of share_m12 (up to 11%, slightly above the knowledge base's ~10% ceiling) is justified partly by 'I1/I2's above-median thumbnail visibility if the fast-follow window ships by mid-year' -- but I1's fast-follow (v1_plus_hero) has no timeline, no tooling schedule, and no FTO-search cost modeled anywhere in this run's fixed_launch_cost_usd or timeline (those are v1_now-scoped only). 'Ships by mid-year' is an unbudgeted, unscheduled assumption doing real work in the optimistic tail of the forecast.
findings.fix: Either drop the I1-fast-follow justification from share_m12's high end since it isn't funded/scheduled this run, or explicitly timeline and cost the v1_plus_hero fast-follow so the assumption is traceable to a real, budgeted plan.

findings.finding: The ERRC 'create' bucket lists 'A physically visible, touchable proof-of-mechanism (the sift window, I1)' as part of the brand's differentiation story without noting it's deferred to v1_plus_hero, not shipping in v1_now. A reader of the ERRC section alone (without cross-referencing version_plan) would assume this ships at launch -- inconsistent with how listing_implications.main_image_brief and image_prompts correctly flag the I1 deferral elsewhere in the same file.
findings.fix: Add a '(v2, fast-follow)' qualifier next to the I1 reference in errc.create so the section is internally consistent with version_plan.v1_now.

three_things_the_founder_must_hear: On genius's own base-case numbers, per-unit contribution comes out negative (about -$0.30, not '25% red flag' or '15% no-go' but below zero) once the blended 42% launch ACoS is actually applied against the $18.99 price -- the founder summary calls this 'close to zero,' which understates a real economics failure on a product already tagged FRAGILE MARGIN. Resolve this before ordering samples.

The main product image spec uses a colored gradient background instead of Amazon's required plain-white primary-image background -- a compliance mistake that could get the hero image rejected or suppressed and would erase the entire grid-standout strategy the plan is built around.

Nearly all the competitor price and image data driving the buying-anchor judgement is Walmart data, not Amazon data, because Amazon pages were blocked this session -- treat the $10.17 anchor and the 'generic white-background rivals' picture as an unverified proxy for the real Amazon page-1 field, not a settled fact, until it can be independently confirmed.
